findings.claim: Replacement compares the NFC upload name by exact path, so on a normalization-sensitive filesystem an NFD-named sidecar is not replaced and a second file with the same track identity appears.
findings.impact: On a Linux or NAS drive holding a sidecar copied from macOS, uploading the corrected subtitle leaves two files. The video lists the same track twice. A later rename or move carries whichever is listed first, so the old text can take the new name while the corrected file stays behind under the old name with only a backend warning. The user then sees the old captions after correcting them.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/upload.py:120 normalizes the name through `validate_filename`, and :134 tests that exact path with `is_file()`. backend/app/services/subtitle.py:83-98 lists both files as the same language and normalizes both paths to the same NFC string, so both track entries serve one file. subtitle.py:119-123 keeps listing order, and :132-136 skips the second file because the first already took the target. backend/tests/test_listing_call_inventory.py:3-6 names this hazard class. `test_a_second_upload_replaces_the_file` uses an ASCII name only. decisions.md:17 walked an NFD rename on the Docker Desktop mount, not an NFD replacement.

perspectives.name: persistence
perspectives.notes: Replacement is atomic and keeps the mode. Row deletion runs after the file lands, with cascades relied on through PRAGMA foreign_keys. What the database does not protect is the old subtitle's content: there is no version or validation step before it is overwritten.

perspectives.name: concurrency
perspectives.notes: Two uploads of one subtitle use separate temp names and the last rename wins, with no torn file. A concurrent carry does not match the temp name. The exists-then-move gap in `move_sidecar_subtitles` is unchanged. The emit runs after the commit, so a reconcile sees the committed row removal.

trajectory: Partly yes, at a much smaller scale than before, and this round also removed one rule. cde9bc7a3 is the only code commit since r4; 5ea567d60 adds tests, and 4e5d2d82c and f08c2dd63 are records. cde9bc7a3 removes the subtitle's 409 and the silent skip of `scan.complete`, both of which r4 reported. It adds one more branch of the kind bd49bc092 added in the previous round, a test for 'is this a subtitle' on the upload path: `replaces_subtitle` at init, joining the branches in `complete_upload` and in the route. So the upload path now special-cases subtitles in three places, and the route's branch repeats the same emit with different counts. It adds no new state, and no prediction of the kind r2 and r3 kept adding; the row state stays removed. The per-sidecar `target.exists()` prediction from r1 is untouched, and its failures stay in the ledger, which gained four more rows this round. On the row strand the design is no longer being patched. The remaining pattern is at the edge of the decision that a subtitle is a file with no record: each capability it lacks is handled by a branch or a ledger row. This round's new findings follow from that, because a file with no record has no version, validation, reindex or folder tracking around it.
